questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q01 Which action best begins integrated portfolio preparation?\

answer.text: A. Decorate the portfolio before checking contents.

feedback.text: Incorrect. First check completeness and purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Submit the first file found.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Selection should be purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. List required parts and mark each present, missing, or needing revision.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear readiness map. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Remove the author statement.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reflection is part of portfolio synthesis. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q02 Which piece belongs in a final portfolio?\

answer.text: A. A revised piece that shows a specific craft skill and reader effect.

feedback.text: Correct. This supports portfolio evidence. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A piece with no title and no revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not reader-ready. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A favorite piece the writer cannot explain.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Preference alone is weak evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A draft with comments still visible.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Draft comments weaken final readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q03 A portfolio statement discusses voice. Which evidence best matches it?\

answer.text: A. A random image pasted beside the title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not show voice development. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A revised story excerpt where dialogue and sentence rhythm reveal character voice.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly supports the stated craft growth.

answer.text: C. A file name with no writing attached.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A file name is not craft evidence.

answer.text: D. A paragraph saying the writer worked hard.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Effort alone does not show voice. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q04 Which portfolio order has the clearest purpose?\

answer.text: A. Alphabetical by file name with no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This may not guide craft understanding. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Random order based on download time.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random order does not support readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Longest to shortest only because length matters most.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length is not the main purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Story first for revised dialogue, poem second for voice through rhythm, statement last to explain growth.

feedback.text: Correct. This order guides the reader through evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q05 Which note is most useful during a readiness pass?\

answer.text: A. Preview script and make character labels consistent.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a specific publication-readiness action.

answer.text: B. Fix it later.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Maybe change something.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not identify the problem. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. It looks fine from far away.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readiness requires specific checks. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q06 How should an author statement connect to selected pieces?\

answer.text: A. It should discuss unrelated goals only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The statement should connect to the work.

answer.text: B. It should hide all revision evidence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision evidence supports growth. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. It should name skills the reader can see in the portfolio.

feedback.text: Correct. The statement and evidence should support each other.

answer.text: D. It should replace the creative pieces.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It explains the pieces; it does not replace them.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q07 Which presentation choice best supports the portfolio?\

answer.text: A. Read the longest excerpt regardless of purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Excerpt choice should be focused. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Choose one excerpt that shows a craft choice connected to portfolio growth.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects presentation and portfolio evidence. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Avoid explaining the excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation needs craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Summarize every assignment from the course.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is too broad. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q08 Which problem should be fixed before final publication?\

answer.text: A. The writer can explain the piece clearly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is a strength, not a problem.

answer.text: B. The portfolio has a clear title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear title supports readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. The author statement names revision growth.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports synthesis. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The final file includes bracketed notes that say add ending later.

feedback.text: Correct. Draft notes show the piece is not final.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q09 What makes a portfolio integrated?\

answer.text: A. The selected pieces, statement, revision evidence, and presentation plan connect to shared growth.

feedback.text: Correct. Integration means the parts work together. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The files are unrelated but colorful.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Visual decoration does not create integration. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. The portfolio has no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Author reasoning is needed. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The presentation ignores the pieces.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presentation should connect to the portfolio.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q10 Which answer best explains reader effect?\

answer.text: A. I put this first because I found it first.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain reader effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I revised the line breaks so the reader pauses before the speaker's decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This names a choice and effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I added random spacing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing does not support readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I like the color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Preference is not reader effect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q11 A student marks "needs revision" beside the presentation plan. What should come next?\

answer.text: A. Ignore the note.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue should be resolved. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Delete the portfolio.

feedback.text: Incorrect. One issue does not require deleting everything.

answer.text: C. Write the exact missing action, such as add listening focus.

feedback.text: Correct. Specific actions guide revision. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Submit without checking.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readiness requires follow-through. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q12 Which choice shows revision evidence?\

answer.text: A. A draft and final version with a note explaining how feedback improved dialogue.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows change and reasoning. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. A blank page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. There is no evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. A final piece with no explanation and no draft trail.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This may not show revision evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. A decoration folder.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration is not revision evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q13 Which author rationale is strongest?\

answer.text: A. I included this because it was easy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Ease is not a strong rationale. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I included this because it is first alphabetically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. File order is not craft rationale. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I included this because I needed another page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Filler is not portfolio evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I included this poem because revising the image pattern made the speaker's change clearer.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects selection, revision, and effect. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q14 Which statement describes publication formatting?\

answer.text: A. Changing the genre completely.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Formatting prepares the genre; it does not automatically change it.

answer.text: B. Preparing the piece with title, spacing, labels, conventions, and file readiness.

feedback.text: Correct. These are reader-facing format concerns. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Avoiding all revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Formatting and revision can both matter. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Refusing to preview the file.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Previewing supports readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q15 What should a student do if the portfolio order feels random?\

answer.text: A. Leave it random.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random order weakens integration. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Remove every piece.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reordering is the better fix. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Create a reader-focused order and explain the reason.

feedback.text: Correct. Purposeful order helps the reader follow the portfolio.

answer.text: D. Add unrelated colors.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Colors do not solve organization. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q16 Which checkpoint response shows mastery?\

answer.text: A. My portfolio order moves from revised story to poem to statement so readers see voice growth across genres.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains order and craft growth. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I am done because I clicked submit.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Submission alone does not show mastery. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I chose whatever was easiest.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Selection should be purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I cannot explain the order.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Mastery includes rationale. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q17 Which final presentation note is strongest?\

answer.text: A. Listen to everything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too broad. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I do not know what to listen for.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The presenter needs focus. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Ignore the excerpt.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The excerpt is central. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Listen for how the clipped dialogue creates tension after the narrator avoids the question.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a clear listening focus. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q18 Which issue is a portfolio completeness problem?\

answer.text: A. The title is clear.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The required author statement is missing.

feedback.text: Correct. A missing required part must be resolved.

answer.text: C. The presentation has a listening focus.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is a strength. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. The revised piece has paragraph breaks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That supports readability. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q19 Why should the student avoid vague notes like "fix portfolio"?\

answer.text: A. They are too detailed.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They are not detailed enough. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. They replace the need for revision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They do not guide revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. They do not identify the exact action needed.

feedback.text: Correct. Specific notes make revision possible. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. They prove mastery.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Mastery requires clear action and reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q20 Which answer best connects publication and presentation?\

answer.text: A. The portfolio shows the final work, and the presentation explains how selected craft choices work.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the relationship between product and author reasoning.

answer.text: B. The presentation should ignore the portfolio.

feedback.text: Incorrect. They should connect. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Publication means no one reads the piece.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication prepares work for readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Presentation means only summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Presentation includes craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q21 Which choice should be removed from a final portfolio file?\

answer.text: A. Clear title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A clear title should remain. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Unresolved comment saying check spelling.

feedback.text: Correct. Unresolved comments make the file look unfinished.

answer.text: C. Intentional line breaks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Purposeful line breaks support poetry. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Author name if required.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Required author information should remain. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q22 Which answer is strongest when explaining a selected excerpt?\

answer.text: A. I selected it randomly.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Selection should be purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I selected it because it is confusing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Confusion does not support audience understanding. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I selected it because it shows the exact revision I describe in my statement.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects excerpt and author reflection. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I selected it but will not explain it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Presentation requires explanation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q23 Which readiness pass checks genre-specific format?\

answer.text: A. Make every genre look identical.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Genres have different format needs. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Remove all titles.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Titles often prepare readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Add random spacing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing distracts. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Check poems for intentional line breaks and scripts for clear character labels.

feedback.text: Correct. Genre-specific formatting supports readers. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q24 A student says the statement and portfolio do not match. What is the best fix?\

answer.text: A. Align the statement's claims with evidence in the selected pieces.

feedback.text: Correct. This creates a coherent portfolio. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Hide the selected pieces.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The portfolio needs evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Delete all reflection.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Reflection is part of the course. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Ignore the mismatch.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Mismatch weakens integration. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q25 Which final decision best shows Unit 6 integration?\

answer.text: A. Submit one rough draft only.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That is incomplete. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Submit a presentation with no portfolio.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The unit requires integrated work. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Submit unrelated files without explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Integration requires purpose and connection. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Submit publication-ready pieces, a connected author statement, revision evidence, and a presentation plan with craft focus.

feedback.text: Correct. This combines the unit's core skills.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q26

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q26 Portfolio context: A writer says, "I chose this poem because I like it." What is the best revision of the selection reason?\

answer.text: A. I chose this poem because it was short.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length alone is not craft evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I chose this poem because I found it first.

feedback.text: Incorrect. File order does not prove portfolio value.

answer.text: C. I chose this poem because the revised final image shows stronger control of imagery and emotion.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives a craft-based reason supported by revision evidence.

answer.text: D. I chose no pieces because portfolios do not need writing.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A portfolio requires selected work. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q27

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q27 Which item is the strongest evidence for a craft rationale?\

answer.text: A. A statement that the piece exists.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Existence is not evidence of craft growth.

answer.text: B. A before-and-after revision that changes "I was lonely" into a specific bus stop image.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows a concrete revision and craft improvement.

answer.text: C. A random font change.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random formatting does not show craft rationale.

answer.text: D. A sentence saying the piece is good.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague praise, not evidence. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q28

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q28 Which three parts belong in a complete craft rationale?\

answer.text: A. Selection claim, evidence, and reader effect.

feedback.text: Correct. These parts explain why the piece belongs in the portfolio.

answer.text: B. Title, font, and file name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. These do not explain craft growth. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Summary, summary, and more summary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A rationale needs evidence and effect, not only summary.

answer.text: D. Favorite line, favorite color, and page number.

feedback.text: Incorrect. These do not form a complete rationale.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q29

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q29 Author statement: "I guess this poem is fine, and people can think whatever." What is the main tone problem?\

answer.text: A. It is too specific and reflective.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The statement is not specific or reflective.

answer.text: B. It explains too much craft reasoning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. It gives almost no craft reasoning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. It sounds uncertain and dismissive.

feedback.text: Correct. The tone does not fit a publication-ready author statement.

answer.text: D. It is too organized.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The statement lacks clear organization. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q30

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q30 Which author statement sentence has the strongest tone?\

answer.text: A. This is good and nobody should question it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sounds defensive and exaggerated. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I wrote stuff and it happened.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is vague and careless. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. People probably will not get it.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This sounds dismissive rather than reflective. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I revised this piece to make the speaker's uncertainty clearer through repeated images.

feedback.text: Correct. The tone is reflective, specific, and publication-ready.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q31

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q31 Story problem: Readers do not understand why Ellis leaves at the end. Which revision best fits?\

answer.text: A. Change Ellis's shirt color.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not clarify motivation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Add one action showing Ellis choosing to leave before the final line.

feedback.text: Correct. This directly clarifies motivation and sequence. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Add random weather description.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Weather does not automatically solve character motivation.

answer.text: D. Delete every character.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This removes the story instead of revising it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q32

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.FIC.06 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q32 Story problem: A suspense scene moves too quickly. Which revision best improves pacing?\

answer.text: A. Add action beats as the character listens at the door and watches the light shift.

feedback.text: Correct. Action beats slow the moment and build suspense.

answer.text: B. Remove the entire scene.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The scene can be revised. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Add a random joke.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That may weaken suspense. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Change every name.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Names do not control pacing. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q33

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q33 Poem problem: The line says, "I felt sad." Feedback asks for a stronger image. Which revision best fits?\

answer.text: A. I felt very sad and sadder.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This repeats the feeling. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Sadness is a feeling.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This defines rather than revises. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Rain gathered on the sill until the glass forgot the street.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses a concrete image to suggest sadness.

answer.text: D. I deleted the poem.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The poem can be revised. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q34

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.POE.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q34 Poem problem: The final choice happens too quickly. Which revision best uses line breaks?\

answer.text: A. Add random breaks after every letter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random breaks distract readers. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Place the final phrase on its own line so the reader pauses before the decision.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses line breaks to control pacing.

answer.text: C. Remove all line breaks forever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Line breaks can support meaning. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Change the poem into a grocery list.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not address pacing. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q35

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q35 A student is preparing a poem for digital publication. Which formatting choice best supports the genre?\

answer.text: A. Put the entire poem in one paragraph so it uses less space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A poem usually needs intentional line breaks and stanza breaks so the reader can follow image, sound, and pacing.

answer.text: B. Add random symbols before every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Decoration can distract readers if it does not support meaning.

answer.text: C. Remove the title because poems do not need one.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title often prepares the reader for the poem's focus or tone.

answer.text: D. Keep the title clear and preserve purposeful line and stanza breaks.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches the poem's genre and helps the reader see how the poem moves.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q36

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q36 A short story draft appears as one long block of text with dialogue inside the same paragraph. What should the writer do first?\

answer.text: A. Add paragraph breaks when the speaker changes and when the action shifts.

feedback.text: Correct. Paragraphing helps readers follow dialogue, action, and pacing in prose.

answer.text: B. Change every sentence to a different font.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font changes do not solve the readability problem.

answer.text: C. Remove all dialogue marks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This would make the dialogue harder to follow.

answer.text: D. Add extra blank lines after every sentence.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random spacing can make the piece look unfinished.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q37

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.WR.08

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q37 An author presentation begins with a short story excerpt. Which opening best prepares the audience?\

answer.text: A. I am reading something I wrote, and that is all you need to know.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs title, genre, and a useful frame.

answer.text: B. My piece is a short story called The Last Bus. Listen for the short sentences because they show panic.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives title, genre, brief context, and a listening focus.

answer.text: C. This is long, so I will explain every event before reading.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Too much summary can overwhelm the presentation.

answer.text: D. I picked this because it is my favorite.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Personal preference alone does not prepare the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q38

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q38 Which excerpt choice is strongest for an author presentation?\

answer.text: A. The longest section, even if it needs ten minutes of explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Long excerpts can make the presentation unfocused.

answer.text: B. A random middle section with no context.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The audience needs a clear entry point.

answer.text: C. A short section that clearly shows a craft choice and can be understood with brief context.

feedback.text: Correct. A focused excerpt helps the audience notice the writer's craft.

answer.text: D. The first page only because first pages are always best.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The best excerpt depends on the presentation purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q39

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.REV.01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q39 Which portfolio choice is strongest?\

answer.text: A. Choose the longest piece only because it fills space.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Length alone does not prove portfolio value.

answer.text: B. Choose the favorite piece with no explanation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A portfolio choice needs evidence and rationale.

answer.text: C. Choose a piece with unresolved draft comments.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Final portfolio work should be reader-ready.

answer.text: D. Choose a revised piece that shows clear craft growth and can be explained.

feedback.text: Correct. This connects selection, revision, and author reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q40

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01 Question ID: CW_U06_UA_Q40 A student notices the author statement discusses imagery, but no selected piece shows imagery. What should the student do?\

answer.text: A. Revise the statement or portfolio so the evidence and explanation match.

feedback.text: Correct. The statement and portfolio should support each other.

answer.text: B. Leave the mismatch because readers will guess.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Readers should not have to guess the connection.

answer.text: C. Remove all craft language from the statement.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Craft language is needed for author reasoning.

answer.text: D. Add random images to every page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random additions do not create purposeful evidence.
